articleSummary: A 14-year-old girl in Xiamen, Fujian, China, presented with persistent lower back pain but no fever. Imaging revealed destruction of the L4 vertebral body with a suspected paravertebral abscess, indicating spinal infection. Routine blood tests showed normal white blood cell count, but erythrocyte sedimentation rate was markedly elevated; tuberculosis was ruled out. Lumbar lesion biopsy demonstrated abundant Staphylococcus aureus, confirming vertebral osteomyelitis caused by S. aureus. The infection was likely seeded through an invasive procedure performed at a clinic, allowing bacteria to invade the spine. Targeted antibiotics led to rapid pain relief and good recovery on follow-up. The report emphasizes that teenage spinal infections are rare and may present without fever, urging thorough evaluation of persistent or progressive back pain (over ~2 weeks) with ESR and MRI, and caution against early invasive therapies such as acupuncture or local injections. Obtaining tissue for culture is essential to guide precise therapy and prevent chronic complications. Keywords: spinal infection, Staphylococcus aureus, vertebral osteomyelitis, adolescent health, invasive procedures.

articleSummary: Plague, caused by Yersinia pestis, is transmitted through rats and rat fleas, notably Xenopsylla cheopis, which parasitize rodents. Three trophic levels—rats, rat fleas, and the bacteria—drive transmission: when an infected rat dies, fleas seek new hosts and can bite humans, introducing the pathogen. While the Black Death devastated Europe, North Africa, and Western Asia in 1347–1351, today plague in Indonesia is limited to several districts on Java and is under ongoing surveillance by the Ministry of Health. Because rats are central to transmission, controlling rodents in residential areas—through sanitation and removing food sources such as trash—remains a key preventive measure. These points were highlighted by IPB University expert Dr Swastiko Priyambodo in statements cited by Liputan6.com.

articleSummary: IPB University’s School of Veterinary Medicine and Biomedical Sciences identified an antimicrobial resistance (AMR) gene in Escherichia coli from the animal slaughter ecosystem in Banten Province, Indonesia. articleSummary: An integrated genomic-epidemiologic study of cholera in Africa analyzes 1762 genomes from 36 countries (1989–2023) and surveillance data from 45 nations (1970–2023). Published in Science, it identifies regional transmission units: two in West Africa and neighbors, a central-east-southern corridor, and a southern cluster; broader epidemiology supports two networks (West Africa and central-to-southern Africa). Transmission declines with distance (88% per 1000 km), but within-unit spread is ~13.5 times higher than between units. AFR10 and AFR9 lineages account for ~46% of Africa’s cholera cases since 1970 (~2.4 million). A Hidden Markov Model combines clinical and genomic data to estimate spread during sampling gaps. Simulations (2000 imports per country) show within-unit outbreaks ~10x likelier in a year; Ghana could seed 4.69 more West African countries, Nigeria 4.33, Cameroon 0.58. Implication: prioritize vaccination in Mozambique if Angola’s outbreak spreads, reflecting network connectivity. Limitations include sampling bias and reliance on suspected cases.

articleSummary: Thai man Tanapathar (aka August), 25, developed monkeypox after four tests; infection likely from sharing a drinking cup at an Oct 9 party, then an Oct 10 event with attendees. Early symptoms included 2–3 days of insomnia, malaise, severe back pain, bowel disturbance, and bilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy, followed by a spreading rash and vesicles on face and body. Despite initial doubts, diagnosis was confirmed after testing. There is no specific antiviral; treatment options include hospital isolation or Bamrasnaradura Institute referral, but he chose home isolation with symptomatic care (antipyretics, analgesics) and remote monitoring for eight days, with a follow-up blood test. Now pain is subsided, fever resolved, lesions crusting; still in isolation. He emphasizes that monkeypox can spread through shared cups, not only sexual contact. Thai DDC reports 470 cases and 3 deaths in Thailand as of Oct 31, 2569; WHO data through Aug 31, 2569 show 68,096 cases and 272 deaths across 107 countries.
notes: 記事はタイ国内の既知のMpox流行（DDC報告：470例、死亡3例、2026年10月31日時点）に関する個別症例の紹介。クレード種別は記事内で明示されていない。コップ共用による非性的接触感染の啓発的側面が強く、新規シグナルというより既存流行の経過報告に近い。

articleHeadline: Santa Catarina tem quarto foco da doença de Newcastle
articleSummary: Fourth Newcastle disease outbreak confirmed in Santa Catarina, Brazil, since the state declared a zoosanitary emergency. The case was detected at a poultry establishment in Nova Erechim, in the western part of the state, within the already restricted area. Surveillance in the emergency zone triggered response protocols: epidemiological investigation, surveillance, and containment; the ministry did not disclose the on-site bird count. Previously, foci were in Nova Itaberaba (Oct 18) and Coronel Freitas (Oct 24) at a farm of about 36,800 turkeys culled; a third outbreak in Nova Erechim involved 9,600 birds that showed no symptoms. The new case makes Nova Erechim have two confirmed foci. All three earlier sites are in sanitary empty periods after cleaning and disinfection. Officials say meat and eggs from officially inspected establishments remain safe. MAPA coordinates with state defense agencies to control the outbreak and protect the national poultry industry.
notes: 本事例はヒトへの直接的健康被害ではなく家禽における動物衛生事象。ただしブラジルは世界有数の鶏肉輸出国であり、貿易制限・輸出停止措置につながる可能性があるため経済的・貿易的観点からPICKUPと判定。人への感染リスク（人獣共通感染症としての影響）は低いとされる。

articleHeadline: 瘟疫再起的信號？中共通報首例死亡病例(圖) - 時評 - 陳靜
articleSummary: China’s CDC quietly released a September 2026 summary showing eight Class A plague cases with one death, but without details on location, age, or transmission, raising concerns of underreporting. The article links this death to broader alarm: on Oct 6, Irkutsk, Russia, an Anti-Plague Research Institute technician reportedly died from plague-related illness; Russia denied “anti-plague measures” and offered to assist the US on infectious diseases. Following online rumors that pneumonic plague had entered China, authorities issued debunking and censored posts. In Chengdu, a Shuangliu District fever clinic patient with high fever reportedly prompted a private warning from a clinician about a recent Russian returnee whose condition deteriorated rapidly—an echo of Li Wenliang’s early whistleblowing. The piece argues this reflects opaque public health reporting, referencing the 2019 Wuhan COVID-19 events, and urges vigilance and preparedness; it is an opinion piece from Look China.
notes: 本記事は意見記事（op-ed）であり、情報源の信頼性に留保が必要。中国CDCの公式発表（ペスト8例、死亡1例、2026年9月分）は事実とされるが詳細非公開。ロシア・イルクーツクでの死亡例、成都での肺ペスト流入の噂は未確認情報であり、検閲対応がなされたとの記述もある。ロシア・米国は対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

articleHeadline: Anthrax Outbreak in Africa's Oldest National Park Is Killing Hippos
articleSummary: Anthrax outbreak in Virunga National Park, the Democratic Republic of Congo, has killed 30 hippopotamuses since September, with the outbreak confirmed by laboratory analyses. This marks the park's second anthrax outbreak since last year. Congo is also contending with an Ebola epidemic that has killed more than 4,800 people since May, straining resources and public health capacity. Health officials note that anthrax outbreaks in the region intersect with food insecurity, conflict, poverty, and disproportionately affect rural populations with limited access to care. Park authorities are raising awareness to prevent contact with or consumption of meat from affected carcasses and to report any finds. Virunga's response focuses on surveillance, safe carcass management, and reducing risks to wildlife and people through documentation of mortalities and coordinated disposal of carcasses.
notes: 記事の主題は動物（カバ）の炭疽病死であり、人間の感染例は報告されていない。同国で進行中のエボラ流行（4800人以上死亡）への言及があり、公衆衛生資源の逼迫状況との関連で背景情報として重要。人間への感染拡大が確認された場合は再評価が必要。
